description: Expanded test set for the retrieval and refusal eval. The ten synthetic documents are unchanged from retrieval-eval.json and the original 110 questions are kept verbatim as a prefix, so the original result stays reproducible as a subset. The added questions are all unanswerable near-misses, each written against one specific document ('nearMissOf') and following the same patterns as the original null questions: an absent study, a promised follow-up that was never reported, a finer detail inside a study that was reported, an administrative fact, an adjacent lab value, a negation, an unrecorded vital, or an unstated dose. Far-misses were deliberately avoided: padding the set with topically distant questions would tighten the confidence interval on correct refusal while biasing the rate upward. No documents were added, so patient-scoped retrieval (ragChain.js passes { patientId }) is unchanged. The discharge summary's antibiotic was corrected from amoxicillin-clavulanate to levofloxacin, intravenous stepped down to oral: the allergy record grades this patient's penicillin reaction as severe, so a penicillin in the discharge summary was an authoring error rather than a cross-document safety case, and nothing in the chatbot reconciles two documents against each other. One agent throughout also avoids an unexplained mid-course class switch. Four unanswerable questions were reworded to name levofloxacin; they stay unanswerable because the summary gives no dose, no intravenous duration and no rationale.

documents.text: Lipid panel, 12 March 2026. Total cholesterol 242 mg/dL (high). LDL cholesterol 165 mg/dL (high). HDL cholesterol 41 mg/dL. Triglycerides 180 mg/dL (borderline high). Comment: elevated LDL; diet changes advised and statin therapy discussed. Repeat lipid panel in three months.

Complete blood count, 12 March 2026. Haemoglobin 10.9 g/dL (low). Haematocrit 33 percent (low). Mean corpuscular volume 76 fL (low). White blood cells 6.8 x10^9/L. Platelets 245 x10^9/L. Impression: microcytic anaemia, likely iron deficiency. Ferritin to follow.

Thyroid function test, 2 April 2026. TSH 6.8 mIU/L (high). Free T4 0.8 ng/dL (low normal). Anti-TPO antibodies positive. Impression: subclinical hypothyroidism, possibly Hashimoto thyroiditis. Recheck TSH in six weeks; consider levothyroxine.

Diabetes review, 20 April 2026. HbA1c 7.4 percent (above target). Fasting plasma glucose 148 mg/dL. Current medication metformin 500 mg twice daily, increased to 1000 mg twice daily. Annual eye screening and foot examination due. Target HbA1c below 7 percent.

Chest X-ray report, 5 May 2026. Indication: persistent cough for three weeks. Findings: patchy consolidation in the right lower lobe. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. Impression: right lower lobe pneumonia. Follow-up film in six weeks after antibiotics.

Discharge summary, 9 May 2026. Admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Treated with intravenous levofloxacin, switched to oral levofloxacin for five more days. Oxygen saturation 97 percent on room air at discharge. Return if fever, breathlessness or chest pain.

Prescription, 21 May 2026. Atorvastatin 20 mg once nightly. Ferrous sulfate 325 mg once daily with orange juice. Vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Avoid taking iron within two hours of levothyroxine or antacids.

Allergy record, updated 1 June 2026. Penicillin: hives and facial swelling in 2019 (severe). Sulfa drugs: rash. Latex: mild contact dermatitis. No known food allergies. Carry an epinephrine auto-injector.

Cardiology consultation, 15 June 2026. Reason: palpitations. ECG shows normal sinus rhythm, heart rate 72. Echocardiogram: left ventricular ejection fraction 60 percent, no valve disease. 24-hour Holter: occasional premature ventricular contractions, benign. Reduce caffeine.

Vaccination record. Influenza vaccine given 10 October 2025. Tetanus, diphtheria and pertussis booster given 3 February 2022. COVID-19 booster given 18 September 2025. Hepatitis B series complete. Pneumococcal vaccine not yet given; recommended.
